p: Thinktank has an outdoor Science Garden, an engineering playground full of giant contraptions that let kids explore forces, motion and machines in the fresh air. It's a great place to let off steam between galleries.

Outside Millennium Point, Eastside City Park is a modern green space with lawns and fountains, perfect for a picnic. Birmingham Back to Backs, run by the National Trust, is a short walk away and gives a fascinating glimpse into the lives of working families in the city over the past two centuries. Book ahead, as tours fill up quickly.
The Library of Birmingham, with its eye-catching facade and rooftop gardens, is another free stop with great views over the city.
Further out, Cadbury World in Bournville is a chocolate-lover's dream, telling the story of Cadbury and the model village built for its workers.
Make your Thinktank visit a success by timing your arrival around a planetarium show, letting younger kids lead the way and saving the Science Garden for a sunny moment.

Birmingham has had a glow-up in recent years, and the area around Millennium Point is a good example, with new buildings, green space and plenty of places to eat within a few minutes' walk. Digbeth's independent food scene is a particular treat, from street food to cosy cafés, so you won't be short of options for lunch. Brum knows how to feed people, and it does it brilliantly.
